arxiv-1508-01127.title: Encoding CSP into CCS (Extended Version) Thanks: Supported by the DFG via project “Synchronous and Asynchronous Interaction in Distributed Systems”. Affiliation: TU Berlin
arxiv-1508-01127.creator: Meike Hatzel, Christoph Wagner, Kirstin Peters, Uwe Nestmann
arxiv-1508-01127.description: Abstract We study encodings from CSP into asynchronous CCS with name passing and matching, so in fact, the asynchronous π \pi -calculus. By doing so, we discuss two different ways to map the multi-way synchronisation mechanism of CSP into the two-way synchronisation mechanism of CCS.

arxiv-2104-03270.title: A Neural Network Approach for High-Dimensional Optimal Control Applied to Multi-Agent Path Finding
arxiv-2104-03270.creator: Derek Onken, Levon Nurbekyan, Xingjian Li, Samy Wu Fung, Stanley Osher, and Lars Ruthotto
arxiv-2104-03270.description: Abstract We propose a neural network approach that yields approximate solutions for high-dimensional optimal control problems and demonstrate its effectiveness using examples from multi-agent path finding. Our approach yields controls in a feedback form, where the policy function is given by a neural network (NN).

arxiv-2302-10601.title: Few-shot Detection of Anomalies in Industrial Cyber-Physical System via Prototypical Network and Contrastive Learning
arxiv-2302-10601.creator: Haili Sun, Lansheng Han ∗, Yan Huang, Chunjie Zhou
arxiv-2302-10601.description: Abstract The rapid development of Industry 4.0 has amplified the scope and destructiveness of industrial Cyber-Physical System (CPS) by network attacks. Anomaly detection techniques are employed to identify these attacks and guarantee the normal operation of industrial CPS. However, it is still a challenging problem to cope with scenarios with few labeled samples.

arxiv-2304-13376.title: Mixed finite element methods for nonlinear reaction-diffusion equations with interfaces
arxiv-2304-13376.creator: Xinran Jin 1 and Jeonghun J. Lee 2
arxiv-2304-13376.description: Abstract . We develop mixed finite element methods for nonlinear reaction-diffusion equations with interfaces which have Robin-type interface conditions. We introduce the velocity of chemicals as new variables and reformulate the governing equations. The stability of semidiscrete solutions, existence and the a priori error estimates of fully discrete solutions are proved by fixed point theorem and continuous/discrete Grönwall inequalities.

arxiv-2401-07708.title: Emergent Gauge Theory in Rydberg Atom Arrays
arxiv-2401-07708.creator: Yanting Cheng, Hui Zhai
arxiv-2401-07708.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yanting Cheng, Hui Zhai. Rydberg atom arrays have emerged as a novel platform exhibiting rich quantum many-body physics and offering promise for universal quantum computation. The Rydberg blockade effect plays an essential role in establishing many-body correlations in this system. In this review, we will highlight that the lattice gauge theory is an efficient description of the Rydberg blockade effect and overview recent exciting developments in this system from equilibrium phases to quantum dynamics.

arxiv-2406-04045.title: On the Diameter of Undirected Cayley Graphs of Finite Abelian Groups
arxiv-2406-04045.creator: Béla Bajnok W. Kyle Beatty
arxiv-2406-04045.description: Abstract Let s s be a positive integer. Our goal is to find all finite abelian groups G G that contain a 2 2 -subset A A for which the undirected Cayley graph Γ ⁡ ( G , A ) \Gamma(G,A) has diameter at most s s .

arxiv-2504-05892.title: Matched Topological Subspace Detector
arxiv-2504-05892.creator: Chengen Liu, Victor M. Tenorio, Antonio G. Marques, Elvin Isufi
arxiv-2504-05892.description: Abstract Topological spaces, represented by simplicial complexes, capture richer relationships than graphs by modeling interactions not only between nodes but also among higher-order entities, such as edges or triangles. This motivates the representation of information defined in irregular domains as topological signals.

arxiv-2505-06287.title: BedreFlyt: Improving Patient Flows through Hospital Wards with Digital Twins
arxiv-2505-06287.creator: Riccardo Sieve, Paul Kobialka, Laura Slaughter, Rudolf Schlatte, Einar Broch Johnsen, Silvia Lizeth Tapia Tarifa
arxiv-2505-06287.description: Abstract Digital twins are emerging as a valuable tool for short-term decision-making as well as for long-term strategic planning across numerous domains, including process industry, energy, space, transport, and healthcare. This paper reports on our ongoing work on designing a digital twin to enhance resource planning, e.g., for the in-patient ward needs in hospitals.

arxiv-2511-11396.title: Modeling the Multi-Wavelength Afterglow of Short Gamma-Ray Bursts with a Plateau Phase
arxiv-2511-11396.creator: Chen Deng, Yong-Feng Huang, Abdusattar Kurban, Jin-Jun Geng, Fan Xu, Xiao-Fei Dong, Hao-Xuan Gao, En-Wei Liang, Liang Li
arxiv-2511-11396.description: Abstract Short gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) exhibiting a plateau phase provide valuable insights into the post-merger activity of their central engines. Although the physical origin of the plateau remains uncertain, the magnetar energy injection model offers a compelling explanation that reproduces the observed temporal and luminosity features.

britannica-1911-aungervyle-richard.description: Article 'Aungervyle, Richard' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 2), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. During his absence from England he was made (1333) dean of Wells. In September of the same year the see of Durham fell vacant, and the king overruled the choice of the monks, who had elected and actually installed their sub-prior, Robert de Graystanes, in favour of Aungervyle. In February 1334 he was made lord treasurer, an appointment he exchanged later in the year for that of lord chancellor.

pmc-10480102.title: Neonatal inguinal hernias containing the uterus: a case report on changes in uterine position
pmc-10480102.creator: Yuki Muta, Akio Odaka, Seiichiro Inoue, Yuta Takeuchi, Yoshifumi Beck
pmc-10480102.description: A female newborn weighing 542 g and delivered at 27 weeks gestation presented with bilateral inguinal hernias while in the neonatal intensive care unit. Ultrasonography confirmed herniation of the uterus into the right inguinal hernia without signs of incarceration. Due to the absence of complications, she was discharged and scheduled for follow-up at the outpatient clinic.

pmc-12564422.title: Plasmonic Nanosensors for EGFR Detection: Optimizing Aptamer-Based Competitive Displacement Assays
pmc-12564422.creator: Alexandra Falamas, Andra-Sorina Tatar, Sanda Boca, Cosmin Farcău
pmc-12564422.description: This study presents a comparative investigation of plasmonic sensing platforms based on colloidal gold nanoparticle (AuNP) suspensions and gold film over nanosphere (AuFoN) solid substrates for the detection of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), an essential biomarker and therapeutic target in oncology. The strategy relies on fluorescence emission modulation of an Atto647N-labeled DNA oligomer competitively bound to an EGFR-specific aptamer.

pmc-12659218.title: The association between health anxiety and frequency of participation in physical education classes and physical activity in Chinese university students
pmc-12659218.creator: Biaoqi Xu, Hamid Amini
pmc-12659218.description: BackgroundHealth anxiety, defined as excessive worry about illness, is increasingly common among university students. It may both reduce engagement in physical activity for some individuals and be alleviated by regular exercise. Psychosocial resources such as self-efficacy, enjoyment, and social support may mediate these relations, but evidence among Chinese university students is limited.

pmc-12716586.title: Incidence of all-cause mortality in prisons: research protocol for a global registry study and systematic literature review with meta-regression analyses
pmc-12716586.creator: Adrian P Mundt, Enzo Rozas-Serri, Benjamín Ignacio Asencio Rojas, Antonio Morales-Rojas, Pablo A Cifuentes-Gramajo, Sofia Alvarado, Gergő Baranyi, Rohan Borschmann, Seena Fazel, Stuart A Kinner
pmc-12716586.description: AbstractIntroductionPeople in prison experience disproportionate health burdens compared with community-based populations, including elevated rates of infectious and non-communicable diseases, mental illness and substance use disorders. Previous studies have consistently shown increased rates of mortality following release from incarceration, particularly from external (unnatural) causes such as suicide and violence.

pmc-12963470.title: Underserved Latinas' Perceptions and Implications Around Breast Cancer Risk Assessment
pmc-12963470.creator: Jane Q Yap, Jhenitza P Raygoza, Valentina Hernandez, Crystal Gonzalez, Celine Vachon, Jessica D Austin
pmc-12963470.description: IntroductionBreast cancer remains a leading cause of death among Latinas. Although breast cancer risk assessment models exist and show promise in reducing mortality, few studies have elicited women's interest in and perceptions around breast cancer risk assessment, particularly among underserved populations, like Latinas, who are susceptible to disparities in breast cancer outcomes.

pmc-13085689.title: Diameter-dependent effects of nanopillar arrays on PEEK bioactivity and soft tissue integration
pmc-13085689.creator: Xi Liu, Yuqi Zhao, Hui Liu, Haochen Wang, Xiaocheng Li, Yixuan Gong, Jie Zheng, Haohan Yu, Chang Su, Wen Song
pmc-13085689.description: Poly-Ether-Ether-Ketone (PEEK) is a promising material for bony structure defects reconstruction due to its favorable mechanical properties and radiolucency. However, its clinical application is limited by poor soft tissue integration resulting from surface bio-inertness. In this study, a highly uniform Nanopillar Array PEEK (NAP) was fabricated using an anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) template-based melt-casting method.

pmc-13208082.title: Nipah virus preparedness in a One Health framework: Implications for Europe
pmc-13208082.creator: Maciej Grzybek, Bartosz Mundt, Ravi Kant, Anna Bogacka
pmc-13208082.description: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic zoonotic henipavirus associated with severe neurological and respiratory disease and a high case fatality rate. Although outbreaks have remained geographically limited, recurrent events in South and Southeast Asia highlight the persistent risk posed by NiV and the potential global consequences of delayed detection and response.

pmc-13335261.title: Antimicrobial resistance and toxin profiles of enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli in children under five years old with diarrhoea in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso: a sentinel surveillance study
pmc-13335261.creator: Alimatou Héma, Issa Tondé, Roger Kaboré, Moussa Sangaré, Mamadou Tamboura, Evariste Bako, Touwendsida Serge Bagre, Marguerite Edith Malatala Nikiema, Aminata Ouattara, M Jahangir Hossain, Subhra Chakraborty, Mahamoudou Sanou
pmc-13335261.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEnterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) remains a major cause of paediatric diarrhoeal disease in sub-Saharan Africa. Increasing antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatens the effectiveness of empirical treatment, yet data on ETEC-specific resistance patterns and toxin profiles in Burkina Faso are scarce.
